nodes.name: Mechanochemical complexation
nodes.procedure: Co-melamine complex with turquoise blue color was synthesized via a mechanochemistry method, in which reddish brown Co(NO3)2·6H2O particles and white melamine powder were ground in a ceramic mortar for 0.5 hr.
nodes.source_text: First, Co-melamine complex with turquoise blue color was synthesized via a mechanochemistry method, in which reddish brown Co(NO3)2·6H2O particles and white melamine powder were ground in a ceramic mortar for 0.5 hr

nodes.name: High-temperature pyrolysis with P precursor
nodes.procedure: The Co/Co2P@NPCNTs was synthesized by pyrolyzing the mixture of Co-melamine complex and triphenylphosphine at 850°C for 2 hrs under N2 atmosphere.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM image shows Co/Co2P nanoparticles with average size of 55 nm encapsulated in intertwined NPCNT skeletons.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1c, the Mott-Schottky Co/Co2P nanoparticles with an average size of 55 nm are encapsulated in the intertwined NPCNT skeletons.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM image shows Co/Co2P nanoparticles encapsulated by NPCNTs with bean-sprout-like structure, most nanoparticles located in nanotube tips.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the TEM image of Co/Co2P@NPCNTs (Fig. 1d) shows that Co/Co2P nanoparticles are encapsulated by NPCNTs, where most of nanoparticles are located in the tips of nanotubes.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM exhibits lattice fringes of 0.35 nm (NPCNTs (002)), 0.205 nm (Co (111)), and 0.218 nm (Co2P (201)) confirming core-shell and Mott-Schottky heterojunctions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The interplanar spacings (d) of 0.35 nm, 0.205 nm, and 0.218 nm can be assigned to the graphitic (002) planes of NPCNTs, (111) planes of Co, and (201) planes of Co2P crystals, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM-EDX elemental mapping shows uniform dispersion of C, N, O, P elements and Co localized in bright-dotted areas.
nodes.evidence_snippet: according to the energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopy and high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) images of Co/Co2P@NPCNTs (Fig. 1f), the C, N, O, and P elements are uniformly dispersed in the catalyst, whereas most of the Co element is localized in the bright-dotted area

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS shows elemental contents of C (64.4 wt%), N (10.1 wt%), O (3.9 wt%), P (5.4 wt%), Co (16.2 wt%) uniformly dispersed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS) mapping (Fig. S3) demonstrates that C, N, O, P, and Co elements are uniformly dispersed on the Co/Co2P@NPCNTs, and the corresponding elemental contents are 64.4, 10.1, 3.9, 5.4, and 16.2 wt%, respectively (Fig. S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms actual Co loading of 17.56 wt% in Co/Co2P@NPCNTs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) was conducted to obtain the actual Co content in Co/Co2P@NPCNTs. As listed in Table S1, the actual loading amount of Co is calculated to be 17.56 wt%

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms co-existence of graphitic carbon ((002) at 26.5°), metallic Co ((111), (200), (220)), and crystalline Co2P ((201), (130), (131)) phases in Co/Co2P@NPCNTs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the XRD patterns of Co@NCNTs and Co/Co2P@NPCNTs reveal an obvious peak at about 26.5°, which corresponds to the (002) planes of graphitic carbon... Co/Co2P@NPCNTs exhibits three additional peaks at 41.1°, 44.1°, and 51.5°, which can be assigned to the (201), (130), and (131) planes of crystalline Co2P phase

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows D-band at 1374 cm⁻¹ and G-band at 1590 cm⁻¹ with ID/IG ratio of 1.17 for Co/Co2P@NPCNTs indicating more defects than Co@NCNTs (0.93).
nodes.evidence_snippet: two apparent peaks centered at 1374 cm⁻¹ and 1590 cm⁻¹... Co/Co2P@NPCNTs yields a higher value of ID/IG ratio than Co@NCNTs (1.17 vs. 0.93), suggesting that more defects and disordered sites are present

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS shows Co⁰ at 778 eV, Co-P at 781.2 eV, Co³⁺ 2p1/2 at 794.1 eV; P 2p: P-Co at 132.6 eV (positive shift), P-C 134.3 eV, P-O 136.1 eV; N 1s: pyridinic N 398.4 eV, pyrrolic N 400.5 eV, graphitic N 402.7 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In high-resolution Co 2p spectrum (Fig. 2d), a strong and sharp peak centered at 778 eV belongs to the Co⁰... peaks centered at 781.2 eV and 794.1 eV can be assigned to the Co-P moieties from Co2P phase and Co³⁺ 2p1/2... P 2p spectrum... apparent peak at 132.6 eV... peaks at about 134.3 eV and 136.1 eV... N 1s spectrum... peaks at 398.4 eV, 400.5 eV and 402.7 eV

nodes.characterization_summary: N₂ adsorption-desorption shows hysteresis loops indicating micropores/mesopores; BET surface area 288 m²/g and pore volume 0.34 cm³/g for Co/Co2P@NPCNTs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The calculated Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) specific surface area and pore volume for Co/Co2P@NPCNTs are 288 m² g⁻¹ and 0.34 cm³ g⁻¹ respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-IR confirms Co-melamine complex formation: Co(NO3)2·6H2O peaks at 1351-1398 cm⁻¹ vanish, melamine peak at 1557 cm⁻¹ shifts to 1540 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: two characteristic peaks of Co(NO3)2·6H2O at about 1351-1398 cm⁻¹ have almost vanished... the peak centered at 1557 cm⁻¹ for melamine is down-shifted to 1540 cm⁻¹ for Co-melamine complex
